What Is Oolong Tea? A Beginner's Guide

2026-10-17 · Tea Types

Oolong (乌龙茶) is a traditional Chinese tea that is partially oxidized — somewhere between unoxidized green tea and fully oxidized black tea. This in-between character gives oolong an extraordinary range of aromas, from floral and creamy to roasted and fruity.

How Oolong Is Made

The defining step is bruising the leaves to start oxidation, then halting it at just the right moment by pan-firing or roasting. Skilled tea makers repeatedly roll and oxidize the leaves to shape them into tight balls or twisted strips.

Flavor Profiles

  • Light oolong (e.g. Tie Guan Yin): floral, fresh, buttery
  • Medium oolong (e.g. Dan Cong): honeyed, orchid-like
  • Dark oolong (e.g. Da Hong Pao): roasted, mineral, deep

Why It Matters

Oolong is central to Chinese tea ceremony culture, especially in Fujian and Guangdong. For beginners, it is a wonderful gateway into the complexity of Chinese tea.
